question: What do the Evolution frames of a TrueHD stream declare of themselves, and what is it worth as a rule?
method: An Evolution frame is the metadata container of ETSI TS 102 366 Annex H as a TrueHD access unit carries it, without the sync word and the length an E-AC-3 skip field puts before it. It declares the version of its syntax, a key identifier and the lengths of two protection words (clauses H.2.2.2.2, H.2.2.2.3, H.2.2.4.1 and H.2.2.4.2). `verify` has counted these since evidence 05 of the verification upgrade and filed one rule, the reserved length code, which had a test and no mutation. It files two more now, at `info`: a version other than 0, and a frame that declares another key identifier or word length than the frame before it. The words themselves are keyed, their computation is not public, and nothing here reads one. `tools/rule_census.py` ran `verify --json` over the streams of the corpus; `tools/sweep.py` ran it over the first minute of every TrueHD and MLP track of a library. The streams are media and are not in the repository.

the_library.what_was_read: the first 60 seconds of each track, cut with `ffmpeg -c copy`

what_a_test_makes_of_the_fixture.another key identifier in one frame: evo.protection_changed twice, into the frame and out of it; exit 0, and 7 at --fail-on info
what_a_test_makes_of_the_fixture.another syntax version in one frame: evo.syntax_version once; no change of protection
what_a_test_makes_of_the_fixture.no primary word and a secondary word of: evo.protection_reserved once, a warning as it was, and evo.protection_changed twice; the frame is as long as it was
what_a_test_makes_of_the_fixture.how: the bits of one frame of the fixture changed and the parity of its extra data put right; the protection words left as they were

each_new_one.mutation: the Evolution frames of a stream not counted for what they declare
an Evolution frame of another syntax version not filed
the rule about another key of an Evolution frame weighing as a warning
an Evolution frame that declares another key counted and not filed
the reserved length of an Evolution frame filed for every frame but the one that codes it
the rule about another syntax version of an Evolution frame failing a stream

checks_on_the_final_state.cargo test --workspace --locked: exit 0; 656 passed, 30 ignored (the media suite, which ran apart)
checks_on_the_final_state.cargo deny check: advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
checks_on_the_final_state.python tools/mutants.py --check: the text of every mutation is in its file

reading: One thing, from the first frame to the last: over 227395 frames of the corpus and 256309 of the library not one declares another key identifier or another length of a word than the frame before it, none codes the reserved length, and none is of another syntax version. The key identifier of the library tracks: 0 on 137. So the two new rules have never fired on a real stream, and neither has the one that was there; all three would mark a stream whose frames changed hands, and stay where they are, two at `info` and the reserved length at `warning`. A minute is the head of a track; what a whole one does at a seamless branch is not in this count.
